metrics.name: correctness
metrics.advice: Run your program on the failing inputs above, especially a match in the last position and an empty array.

metrics.name: syntax
metrics.advice: Fix every compiler warning; compile with -Wall -Wextra to see them.

metrics.name: structure
metrics.advice: Keep each function short and simple, and fix what cppcheck reports.

metrics.name: modularity
metrics.advice: Move the search into a helper function, for example int find_first(const int *values, int n, int target), and call it from main.

metrics.name: logical
metrics.advice: Test an empty array (n = 0), a single number, a match in the last position and repeated values.

reasons.n_zero: wrong result for an empty array (n = 0); check n before reading any element
reasons.single_found: wrong result when the only number is the target; check the loop bounds
reasons.single_missing: wrong result when the only number is not the target
reasons.last_only: the target is the last number but was not found; the loop probably stops one step early (i < n - 1)
reasons.all_duplicates: every number is the target; the answer is the first index, 0
reasons.int_limits: wrong result with INT_MIN or INT_MAX in the array
reasons.target_is_n: the target equals n; the program may be mixing up n and the target
reasons.not_found_large: 1000 numbers and no match; the answer must be -1

metrics.name: complexity
metrics.advice: Look at each number once from left to right; sorting first costs more than the search itself.

metrics.name: memory_safety
metrics.advice: Never read past the end of the array, free what you allocate, and handle n = 0.

metrics.name: readability
metrics.advice: Use clear names, consistent indentation and a short comment above each function.

metrics.name: originality
metrics.advice: Write the solution yourself and be ready to explain every line.

usefulness.use_case: Explaining a wrong answer to the student
usefulness.example: search_off_by_one.c prints -1 when the target 8 is the last of 8 numbers. The report shows the input, the expected 7, and says the loop probably stops one step early (i < n - 1).
usefulness.benefit: The student sees the exact input that breaks the program and the likely line to fix.

usefulness.use_case: Catching a correct but slow solution
usefulness.example: search_sort.c passes all 8 tests and all 8 edge cases, but it bubble sorts first and times out at n = 100000, so it gets 0 for complexity.
usefulness.benefit: Tests alone would give full marks; the timing shows the algorithm is O(n^2).

limitations.limitation: O(n log n) passes as O(n)
limitations.example: A version that sorts with qsort and then does a binary search measured a growth of 0.69, the same as search_good.c, and was judged O(n). Reading the input takes most of the time.
limitations.mitigation: The report gives the measured growth, so a teacher can read the code to check the class.

limitations.limitation: A crash at a large size looks like a slow program
limitations.example: search_crash.c is O(n), but its recursion is a million calls deep at n = 1000000 and runs out of stack. The report says it is slower than O(n) or broken.
limitations.mitigation: The evidence in the JSON report shows the status was a crash, not a timeout.
